page: Microsoft Azure B4als_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Basv2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance asymmetry. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core tests, and average on Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tasks. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory performance is also constrained, with PassMark memory scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 10% of tested systems.

The burstable CPU allocation model offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with variable resource demands, allowing users to pay for lower baseline performance while retaining the ability to burst during peak activity. The primary tradeoff is the limited 8.0 GB memory capacity and weak multi-threaded scaling. This server is best suited for lightweight workloads such as low-traffic web serving, basic text processing, microservices, and development or testing environments that do not require sustained multi-core compute or high memory bandwidth.
